Methods: We trained a population-level Gaussian process emulator whose inputs included a 12-dimensional latent encoding of the clinical features of each patient, so that a single emulator represents the whole cohort. We compared spending simulation budgets on resampling the real cohort with augmenting the cohort with digital chimeras, synthetic patients interpolated between real patients. Seven parameters of a closed-loop heart and circulation model were calibrated by Markov chain Monte Carlo to ten clinical biomarkers in 26 patients with left bundle branch block, each using an emulator trained without that patient, and the calibrated posteriors were compared against the full simulator. Results: A single emulator, trained without the held-out patient, calibrated the digital twin of each patient in 59.7-63.0 s per patient, versus 15 h with the simulator. Resampling the real cohort was the more efficient training strategy, bringing every output to R2 greater than or equal to 0.9, which augmentation did not achieve for the same simulation budget. For held-out patients, both strategies performed comparably (median leave-one-out normalized root-mean-square error 11.0% vs. 10.7%; p = 0.745), and error rose with distance from the cohort centroid (Spearman rho = +0.406). The calibrated models showed no cohort-wide bias (median standardized residual -0.12 against the clinical targets), and 95% predictive intervals contained 78.5% of targets, with the largest misfit in systolic blood pressure. Conclusion: Removing the need for new simulations for every new patient is a meaningful step toward uncertainty-aware cardiac digital twins that fit within a routine clinical workflow. Because the simulator, surrogate and sampler are interchangeable, the approach used here can be applied to other (cardiac) models and cohorts.
na8ff4cead1d3: GBA1 variants are major Parkinson's disease risk factors, but their detection is challenging. We compared NeuroBooster Array (NBA) genotyping with reference sequencing in 3,744 individuals. NBA correctly identified 520/608 carriers (85.5%). Of 89 missed calls, 73 had no matching probe and 16 had missing calls. 25 participants had false positive calls. NBA should not be used alone for clinical decisions, but is very useful for case control analysis.
n0d900b727d94: Diabetic kidney disease is the leading cause of kidney failure worldwide, yet the molecular events underlying disease initiation and progression remain unclear. We measured 5,420 circulating proteins in 830 adults with type 1 diabetes and examined their longitudinal associations with onset and progression of kidney disease over 10 years of follow-up. We identified 130 proteins associated with at least one outcome independent of established clinical risk factors, of which 59 replicated in an independent cohort. HAVCR1/KIM-1, GFRA1, CD14 and GDF15 predicted albuminuria onset up to a decade before detectable disease. Albuminuria progression pointed to the kidney--liver axis (ASGR1, RBP4), whereas rapid kidney function decline and incident kidney failure pointed to immune and tumor necrosis factor receptor signaling. Mendelian randomization prioritized UMOD, SORT1, CLSPN, MAST4 and EGF as potential targets. These findings reveal molecular perturbations preceding clinical manifestations of diabetic kidney disease and identify distinct pathways associated with disease progression.
n8028aaeec4a7: Objective: To describe the role of hysterectomy in modifying the major atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk factors. Data sources: PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, and ScienceDirect were searched from database inception to March 10, 2026. Study eligibility criteria: Full-text randomized controlled trials, case-control studies, cross-sectional studies, cohort studies, case series, and experimental studies reporting new-onset cardiovascular events, diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia, or other metabolic effects following hysterectomy were eligible. Reviews and book chapters were excluded. Study appraisal and synthesis methods: Study selection and data extraction were performed independently by multiple reviewers with conflicts resolved by consensus. Cohort study quality was assessed with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale; a modified version assessed cross-sectional studies. Meta-analyses were performed using a generic inverse-variance random-effects model for each outcome, stratified by study design (cross-sectional versus cohort) and effect measure (adjusted odds ratio, adjusted hazard ratio, or relative risk). Narrative synthesis was performed for outcomes not meeting criteria for meta-analysis. Results: Twenty studies (11 cohort, 8 cross-sectional, 1 mixed design) were included after screening 18,337 records from four databases. Hysterectomy was associated with significantly increased risk of hypertension (cross-sectional odds ratio 1.32, 95% confidence interval 1.18-1.48; cohort hazard ratio 1.19, 95% confidence interval 1.09-1.30), diabetes (cross-sectional odds ratio 1.21, 95% confidence interval 1.11-1.32; cohort hazard ratio 1.20, 95% confidence interval 1.13-1.29), hyperlipidemia (hazard ratio 1.21, 95% confidence interval 1.13-1.29), obesity (odds ratio 1.24, 95% confidence interval 1.03-1.50), and metabolic syndrome (odds ratio 1.24, 95% confidence interval 1.08-1.44). Conclusions: Hysterectomy is associated with increased risk of hypertension, diabetes, hyperlipidemia, obesity, and metabolic syndrome, key modifiable atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk factors. Active cardiovascular risk assessment and follow-up may be warranted for women who undergo hysterectomy, particularly at a young age.
nc61f079f72db: Background: The 2024-25 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey (EDHS) is Ethiopia's first national survey to measure early childhood development using UNICEF's Early Childhood Development Index 2030 (ECDI2030). This provides a national estimate for Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) indicator 4.2.1, the proportion of children aged 24-59 months who are developmentally on track. We estimated the prevalence of being developmentally on track and examined its child, maternal, household and community determinants in Ethiopia. Methods: This cross-sectional study analysed 3,731 children aged 24-59 months (weighted n = 3,514) of 3,232 mothers in 771 clusters. Children were on track if they achieved the age-specific minimum number of the 20 ECDI2030 milestones. Prevalence was estimated with design-based methods. Four three-level mixed-effects logistic regression models (children within mothers within clusters) were fitted, and interviewer effects were assessed. Results: Overall, 36.3% (95% CI 33.4-39.3) of children were developmentally on track. Prevalence ranged from 23.3% in Southwest Regional State, Ethiopia, to 77.7% in Addis Ababa. In the null model, 21.5% of the variation lay between clusters (median odds ratio 3.24). In the final model, the odds of being on track were lower at 36-47 months (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 0.57, 95% CI 0.44-0.74) and 48-59 months (AOR 0.39, 0.30-0.51) than at 24-35 months. They were also lower after a preceding birth interval under 24 months (AOR 0.75, 0.57-0.99), after recent diarrhoea, fever or cough (AOR 0.59, 0.45-0.77), and where distance to a health facility was a big problem (AOR 0.61, 0.48-0.79). Odds were higher for girls (AOR 1.38, 1.12-1.70), with maternal education (more than secondary vs none: AOR 2.08, 1.19-3.63) and with weekly media exposure (AOR 2.15, 1.51-3.06). The covariates explained 55.9% of the between-cluster variance. Conclusions: Nearly two in three Ethiopian children aged 24-59 months are not developmentally on track, and children fall further behind as they age. Interventions should target maternal education, access to information and health services, birth spacing and childhood illness, with priority for the lowest-performing regions and communities.
n73854b165dab: Individuals with Down syndrome (DS) present with both increased rates of autoimmunity and immunodeficiency. To understand this paradox, we first examined lymph node (LN) architecture and immune cell composition in infants with and without DS, as well as peripheral blood B cells from unrelated adults with and without DS. Most strikingly, LNs from individuals with DS exhibited a marked paucity of germinal centers compared with typical lymph nodes. Stromal cells within DS LNs expressed significantly lower levels of the adhesion molecules ICAM1 and VCAM1, accompanied by significantly reduced CXCR5 expression within B cell follicles, suggesting impaired B cell migration and follicular organization. Although fibroblastic reticular cells (FRCs) were present at comparable frequencies in DS and control LNs, MARCO lymphatic endothelial cells (MARCO-LECs), another critical stromal cell population supporting LN architecture, were significantly reduced. In addition, follicular dendritic cells (FDCs), which are essential for antigen retention and B cell selection within germinal centers, were also substantially reduced. To determine the consequences of these abnormalities on humoral immunity, we performed paired single-cell RNA sequencing and V(D)J sequencing of peripheral blood B cells from adults with and without DS. DS memory and CD86⁺ switched memory B cell populations exhibited significantly elevated reactive oxygen species and PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling gene signatures, coupled with reduced levels of somatic hypermutation in the memory population and increase usage of the autoreactivity-associated IGHV4-34 heavy-chain gene. Collectively, these findings suggest that early-life disruption of LN architecture, characterized by reduced expression of adhesion molecules, selective loss of MARCO-LECs, and depletion of FDCs, impairs germinal center function and B cell education. This defective microenvironment likely contributes to inadequate affinity maturation, as reflected by diminished somatic hypermutation and a more autoreactive B cell repertoire in adults with Down syndrome.
n13dd914decf3: To develop and validate a model that predicts on day 7 of subacute rehabilitation (timed to inform the first multidisciplinary team meeting) the probabilities of three mutually exclusive outcomes: minimal dependency, nursing-care dependency, or medical deterioration. Design : Retrospective cohort study with temporal validation. Multinomial regression and XGBoost models were trained on 80% of admissions during the years 2016-2024 of members of the largest national health maintenance organization (HMO), tested on the remaining 20% and members of other HMOs, and validated on year 2025 admissions. Models output patient-level outcome probabilities with the strongest feature contributors. Setting : A public geriatric rehabilitation hospital. Participants: All consecutive first admissions (N=10,920; median age 80 years; median length of stay 35 days). Interventions : Not applicable. Main Outcome Measures : Discharge disposition: minimal dependency, nursing-care dependency, or medical deterioration (transfer to acute care without return, or in-hospital death). Predictors were demographic, functional, cognitive, clinical, and laboratory variables documented before day 7 with linkage to pre-admission community health records. Performance was assessed by multiclass area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), Brier score and positive predictive value (PPV). Results : Overall, 34% of patients were discharged with minimal dependency, 44% with nursing-care dependency, and 22% deteriorated medically. Both models performed comparably. Multinomial regression achieved an AUC of 0.81 (95% CI: 0.79-0.83) compared with 0.72 (0.71-0.73) for FIM alone, and it was maintained on temporal validation (AUC 0.80, 0.78-0.82). At a ≥60% probability threshold, the model flagged 32% of patients for nursing-care dependency and 5% for deterioration, with PPVs of 72% and 69%, respectively. Conclusions : Day-7 multiclass risk estimation from routinely collected data is feasible, interpretable and stable over time. Alerts could prompt earlier social-work involvement and closer monitoring of patients at risk of deterioration; prospective controlled evaluation is warranted.
nd6d57bdc0882: Aims: Diastolic dysfunction in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy reflects changes in sarcomeric function, electrophysiology, ventricular structure, and myocardial mechanics. Their effects on filling remain difficult to determine clinically. We sought to dissect these effects in MYH7-related non-obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy progression. Methods and results: We developed a human biventricular electromechanical model linking electrophysiology and calcium handling to contraction, ventricular mechanics, haemodynamics, electrocardiography, and myocardial strain. Stage I represented MYH7 sarcomeric dysfunction before hypertrophy; Stage II added septal hypertrophy; Stage III added increased myocardial stiffness. Secondary ionic remodelling was examined at each stage and severity. Sarcomeric dysfunction alone generated a low-volume hypercontractile phenotype before overt hypertrophy. Septal hypertrophy further constrained chamber filling, whereas myocardial stiffening exacerbated diastolic dysfunction and regional mechanical heterogeneity. Secondary ionic remodelling produced marked repolarisation abnormalities but, importantly, also prolonged calcium-tension dynamics and impaired relaxation, reducing ventricular filling to an extent comparable with structural remodelling in some disease states. Increasing ionic-remodelling severity progressively amplified these effects. Despite preserved ejection fraction throughout progression, ventricular volumes decreased while global and regional myocardial deformation deteriorated. Conclusion: Diastolic dysfunction was evident before overt hypertrophy and worsened as structural, mechanical, and ionic abnormalities were added. Preserved ejection fraction did not reflect reduced ventricular filling or deterioration in myocardial strain. Regional mechanical measures may therefore reveal disease burden not captured by ejection fraction alone. By separating individual disease mechanisms, in silico modelling may help link measurable biomarkers to their underlying causes and support mechanism-based patient stratification.
n849a0e3b82e5: Background Binge eating disorder (BED) is associated with obesity as well as behavioral and neurobiological changes in the reward and cognitive control systems of the brain. To better dissociate neural mechanisms of pathological eating behavior, functional connectivity (FC) analyses have shown promise. However, there is currently no replicable signature of BED derived from fMRI. Methods We investigated FC in 61 women with varying symptoms of binge eating. The three groups included 21 women with BED, 20 women with subsyndromal BED (subBED), and 20 controls without binge eating (noBE) matched in body mass index (BMI) and age. To identify neural signatures of BED and BMI, we used seed-based FC fingerprints (nucleus accumbens, NAcc, for reward and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, dlPFC, for cognitive control) to predict group or BMI based on resting state and task-based (food bidding) FC. Furthermore, we explored spatial patterns of FC to quantify associations with BED and BMI. Results Both seeds of the reward and cognitive control networks robustly predicted BMI (rs = .33 - .46). The dlPFC seed predicted BMI across conditions (resting state: p=.002; task: p=.012) while the NAcc seed only predicted BMI based on task-based FC (p=.007). In contrast, FC failed to classify binge eating groups better than chance. Conclusions FC within reward and cognitive control networks primarily reflect obesity-related changes. Despite pronounced differences in eating behavior, BED could not be reliably dissociated from subBED or noBE using FC fingerprints. These results highlight challenges in identifying BED-specific functional markers.
n5352e9be70d2: Background: Population-based data on functional difficulty among school-age children in Ethiopia are scarce. The 2024-2025 Ethiopia Demographic and Health Survey (EDHS) included, for the first time, the UNICEF/Washington Group Child Functioning Module (CFM) for children aged 5-17 years. We estimated the prevalence and domain distribution of functional difficulty and associated factors in Ethiopia. Methods: We analysed cross-sectional EDHS data from 11,122 children aged 5-17 years (weighted n = 10,726) and 4,739 mothers. Functional difficulty was defined as "a lot of difficulty" or "cannot do at all" in any of 11 domains, or daily anxiety or depression. We estimated design-based prevalence and fitted multilevel logistic regression models (children within mothers within clusters) for any, non-affective and affective difficulty. Interviewer effects were examined with random-intercept models and within-cluster comparisons. Results: Overall, 9.5% (95% CI 8.1-11.1) of children had functional difficulty. Daily depression (6.8%) and anxiety (6.6%) dominated, and 70.3% of affected children had only affective difficulty. Difficulty in at least one non-affective domain affected 2.8% (2.2-3.7), with each domain at 0.5-1.4%. Prevalence ranged from 1.5% in Southwest Regional State, Ethiopia, to 16.5% in Oromia Regional State. In adjusted models, children not attending school had higher odds of non-affective difficulty (AOR 2.82, 95% CI 2.01-3.96), and girls had lower odds (AOR 0.63, 0.48-0.84). Outcomes clustered strongly within families (sibling correlation 67.7%) and clusters (ICC 20.9%). Six of 163 interviewers (7.9% of the weighted sample) contributed 58.2% of weighted cases of daily anxiety or depression; in the same clusters they recorded daily symptoms for 56.4% of children, against 2.1% for other interviewers. Excluding 11 statistically outlying interviewers reduced the prevalence of any difficulty to 4.6% (3.6-5.8) and of daily anxiety or depression to 3.3%. The associations with school non-attendance and sex were unchanged. Conclusions: Functional difficulties across the sensory, physical, cognitive, and affective domains, including anxiety or depression, affect about 2-3% of Ethiopian children aged 5-17 years and are strongly associated with being out of school. Appropriate interventions and resource allocation should be considered.
nbf3ac4355565: Objectives Modic changes (MC) are vertebral endplate and bone marrow lesions strongly associated with chronic low back pain. Type 1 MC (MC1, oedema-like) and type 2 or 3 MC (MC2or3, fat- and sclerosis-like) are commonly regarded as different stages of the same pathological process, yet their underlying biology remains poorly defined. In particular, it remains unclear whether MC are confined to the spine or accompanied by distinct systemic immune alterations. Here, we provide the first comprehensive characterisation of the circulating immune landscape in patients with lumbar MC. Methods Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were analysed from 37 patients undergoing lumbar spinal surgery: 11 with no MC, 15 with MC1 and 11 with MC2or3. Samples were fluorescently barcoded, pooled, and stained with a 28-antibody phenotyping panel. Each pool was then split into 30 aliquots, and each of these was co-stained with a different PE-conjugated anti-integrin, -selectin, or -chemokine receptor antibody or isotype controls. Differences in abundance were tested with binomial mixed models adjusted for acquisition batch, age, and sex. Differentially abundant compartments were clustered by FlowSOM and the same binomial model was used to test differences in cluster abundance. Adhesion receptors were analysed as single chains. Results The {gamma}{delta} T cell compartment was the only population significantly expanded in MC patients (median 0.58% of all recorded cells in nonMC donors versus 1.61% in pooled MC (OR = 2.38, q = 0.035)). Clustering {gamma}{delta} T cells into subsets showed compartment-wide expansion, primarily driven by V{delta}2+ T cells. The adhesion receptor screen revealed 6 and 2 integrin on basophils, endoglin on plasmacytoid dendritic cells, and {beta}7 integrin on IgA B cells as differentially expressed in MC, but none survived multiple-testing correction across the whole screen. Conclusions Lumbar MC are accompanied by expansion of circulating {gamma}{delta} T cells. This aligns with previously reported {gamma}{delta} T cell accumulation in MC1 lesions, underscoring the role of {gamma}{delta} T cells in MC pathophysiology.
n200533a53323: Introduction: Socioeconomic differences in body mass index (BMI) are well established, but less is known about gender differences and their behavioral pathways. We examined gender differences in the association between socioeconomic position (SEP) and BMI, and whether dietary factors and physical activity mediated the associations. Methods: We used survey data from the employees of the City of Helsinki aged 19-39 collected in 2017 (n = 4,400, 80% women). SEP was measured by highest educational attainment, and the examined mediators were consumption of fruit and vegetables, red and processed meat, sweets and confectionery and alcohol as well as leisure-time vigorous physical activity (VPA) and sedentary time. We conducted gender-specific multiple mediation analyses using structural equation modeling and additional analyses using multiple imputation by chained equations. Results: With increasing educational attainment, mean BMI decreased from 26.4 kg/m2 to 24.0 kg/m2 among women, and from 26.6 kg/m2 to 25.2 kg/m2 among men. Lower SEP was associated with lower consumption of fruit and vegetables, higher consumption of red and processed meat, and lower VPA in both genders. Women reported healthier diets but less VPA than men. The strongest SEP-BMI mediator among women was VPA (indirect effect: 0.35, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.26, 0.44), followed by fruit and vegetable consumption (0.15, 95% CI 0.08, 0.23) and red and processed meat consumption (0.06, 95% CI 0.02, 0.11). Among men, significant mediators were red and processed meat consumption (0.12, 95% CI 0.03, 0.23), sedentary time (0.11, 95% CI 0.01, 0.24) and VPA (0.10, 95% CI 0.02, 0.21). Conclusions: Socioeconomic inequalities in BMI appear stronger among women and are shaped through partly different mechanisms between genders. Improving VPA may be relevant among low-SEP women, whereas reducing sedentary time may be more relevant among low-SEP men. Reducing red and processed meat is beneficial for both genders.
nee73631eaa93: Background and Objectives: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neurological disorder characterized by demyelination and neuroaxonal injury. MS genetic susceptibility and severity long after disease onset is well characterized, but the genetic architecture of disability severity near disease onset is unclear. We performed the first genome-wide association study of early MS severity to identify causal loci, prioritize effector genes and associated pathways, and understand the relationships of early MS severity and various traits. Methods: The primary outcome was the first age-related MS severity score (ARMSS), an age-adjusted severity measure, in 7,209 individuals of Swedish discovery cohorts and independent Italian and multi-national European replication cohorts. Replicated loci underwent conditional analysis, fine-mapping, time-to-event MS phenotype association analyses, and multi-omics-based gene prioritization. Using the genome-wide summary statistics, we also conducted heritability analyses, polygenic risk score association with other MS phenotypes, gene-level and pathway analyses, cross-trait analyses with disease-related traits, Mendelian randomization, and drug-repurposing screening. Results: Two suggestive loci were replicated: rs1234317 at chromosome 1 (effect allele T: beta = 0.100, SE = 0.0189, P = 1.08E-07) and rs929769 at chromosome 5 (effect allele T: beta = -0.0956, SE = 0.0184, P = 1.95E-07). Fine-mapping supported rs929769 as a single-variant 95% credible set, and rs1234317 and rs6657136 as a two-variant 95% credible set with two-causal-SNP model having the highest posterior probability. The SNPs did not show a significant change in effect sizes when adjusted for heritable traits and exhibited attenuated associations with long-term MS disability progression. TNFSF4 was the top prioritized effector for rs1234317, TNFSF18 for rs6657136, and ADAMTS2 for rs929769. Early MS severity showed partial genetic overlap with MS susceptibility or late MS severity, but no significant correlation with a range of neurological, psychiatric, autoimmune, cognitive, and aging traits. Pathway analyses identified ion-channel regulation and folic acid metabolism, and Mendelian randomization suggested nominal bidirectional associations with educational attainment. Drug screening nominated several drugs that can be repurposed. Discussion: This study identifies candidate causal variants of early MS severity and their effector genes: TNFSF4, TNFSF18, and ADAMTS2. It provides insights into the genetic architecture and therapeutic measures for the early phase of MS severity.
n274c839aa39a: Objective. Patients often describe menstrual-cycle worsening of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD). We prospectively evaluated sample- and person-level cycle effects on ADHD symptoms and their independence from cyclical negative affect and pain. Methods. In an intensive longitudinal cohort (2019-2024), 106 naturally cycling adults meeting DSM-5 ADHD criteria on integrated assessment rated daily inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity (Barkley Adult ADHD Rating Scale-IV), negative affect, and pain (median, 41 days) and provided daily salivary estradiol and progesterone for ovulation coding and phase-aligned cycle time (PACTS). Generalized additive models estimated sample-level and person-specific cycle curves; robust cyclicity was tested against each participant's own time-shuffle null. Lab cognitive testing at four counterbalanced phases provided post hoc validation. Results. Sample-average cycle effects were significant yet small (<1% of daily variance), but 54% of 87 participants tested individually were robustly cyclical in ADHD symptoms (95% CI, 44%-64%; inattention 43%, hyperactivity-impulsivity 26%), more often with informant-confirmed ADHD (69% vs 36%). Among them, the cycle explained median 52% and 51% of symptom variance, a mean swing of 2.6 and 2.1 DSM-5 criteria. Most remained cyclical after adjustment for affect (68%) or pain (81%). Worsening most often peaked at and after menses rather than premenstrually; no cycle met prospective criteria for premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD). Hormones did not differ by cyclicity. Conclusions. About half of these adults with ADHD showed robust cyclical symptom change, mostly not reducible to cyclical affect or pain and usually outside the premenstrual window. Future work should test its stability and whether a DSM-5 cyclical specifier is warranted.
n8922fe1a564f: Background: The MUC5B promoter variant (rs35705950) is the strongest common genetic risk factor for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF). MUC5B and MUC5AC contain variable number tandem repeat (VNTR) regions. Long-read sequencing resolves MUC5AC into three SNP-tagged haplogroups (H1, H2, H3) differing in repeat length, and MUC5B into two (H1, H2) differing in lineage but not length. The tags correlate with rs35705950, so whether a haplogroup effect is distinguishable from the promoter variant is unclear. Methods: We assigned MUC5AC and MUC5B haplogroups from imputed chromosome 11 array data in 771 European-ancestry IPF Job Exposures Study participants (385 cases, 386 controls). Logistic regression adjusted for age, smoking, principal components and centre, with and without rs35705950. The same models were fitted in TOPMed (1,961 cases, 3,816 controls). Results: MUC5AC H3 and MUC5B H1 were each associated with IPF (H3 OR 1.63, 95% CI 1.26-2.09, p=1.8x10-4; MUC5B H1 OR 0.71, 0.52-0.98, p=0.038). Both attenuated on adjustment for rs35705950 (H3 OR 1.10, 0.83-1.45, p=0.52; MUC5B H1 OR 0.82, 0.58-1.15, p=0.25). A MUC5AC H2 association persisted after adjustment (OR 0.69, 0.51-0.94, p=0.017). In TOPMed the H3 findings replicated (unadjusted OR 1.62, 1.47-1.78, p<10-15; adjusted 0.94, 0.84-1.05, p=0.26), but the rs35705950-adjusted H2 association did not: the estimate was null overall (OR 0.99, 0.88-1.11, p=0.87) and in men and women separately (1.00, 0.87-1.16; 0.97, 0.79-1.19). The MUC5B tag failed quality control in TOPMed. Conclusions: The MUC5AC H3 and MUC5B H1 associations are not independent of rs35705950. The MUC5AC H2 association seen here did not replicate. VNTR haplogroup does not appear to contribute to IPF risk independently of rs35705950.
ncab9f64273c3: Background: TB eradication strategies in high burden countries need affordable, scalable, and accessible screening tools. This study investigated the diagnostic accuracy of C-reactive protein (CRP), serum amyloid A (SAA), and interferon gamma-induced protein 10 (IP-10) as potential screening tools. Methods. This cross-sectional diagnostic study investigated stored archived serum samples from three groups of subjects; bacteriology confirmed symptomatic TB group (n=57), probable TB (n=56) and healthy controls (n=60). CRP and SAA concentrations were measured using near point-of-care fluorescence immunoassay (NPOCT-FIA), while IP-10 was measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Diagnostic performance of individual and combined biomarkers was evaluated Results Receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance of serum amyloid A (SAA) and C-reactive protein (CRP) for identifying confirmed tuberculosis (TB). Compared with probable TB and healthy controls, SAA achieved an AUC of 0.961 (cut-off >31.0 mg/L), with 96.5% sensitivity and 88.6% specificity, while CRP achieved an AUC of 0.953 (cut-off 21.3 mg/L), with 96.5% sensitivity and 86.0% specificity. Interferon gamma-induced protein 10 (IP-10) showed poor discrimination (AUC 0.545). Combined CRP and SAA achieved 100.0% sensitivity and 83.3% specificity. Conclusion: SAA and CRP met WHO target product profile criteria for TB triage screening.
n6bccf130b402: Background There is limited research on persistent or recurrent depression into young adulthood. We examined the prevalence of recurrent/persistent depression in young adults, and associations with childhood trauma/adversity and systemic inflammation, and if inflammatory markers mediated associations between childhood trauma and subsequent depression. Methods ALSPAC participants with ICD-10 depression assessments at ages 18, 24 and 30 were classified as never depressed, transiently depressed (one episode), or persistently/recurrently depressed ([≥] 2). Trauma/adversity from birth to age 16/17 was characterised by type, timing and burden. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) and C-reactive protein (CRP) were measured at ages 9, 16, 18 and 24. Analyses used multinomial logistic regression, linear regression and causal mediation models. Results Among 2,014 participants, 78.9% were never depressed, 15.0% had transient depression and 6.1% had persistent/recurrent depression. Trauma/adversity was more strongly associated with persistent/recurrent depression (RRR 3.17, 95% CI 1.98-5.06; FDR-P=6.2x10^-6) than transient depression, with a dose-response pattern and stronger associations for threat adversities. Middle-to-late childhood (11-17 yrs) emerged as a sensitive period for persistent/recurrent (RRR 2.85, 95% CI 1.47-5.52) and transient depression (RRR 1.85, 95% CI 1.25-2.73). Trauma/adversity was associated with modestly higher IL-6 at age 24 (all FDR-adjusted P < 0.05); CRP associations did not survive multiple-testing correction. Neither marker mediated trauma/adversity associations with persistent/recurrent depression. Conclusion Persistent/recurrent depression affects approximately 1 in 20 young adults. Childhood trauma/adversity, particularly during middle-to-late childhood, was associated with persistent/recurrent depression, but measured inflammatory proteins did not mediate this association. Further work is needed to understand biological mechanisms underlying the embedding early life psychosocial stress.
naaf366bc1705: Whole-genome sequencing identifies large numbers of genetic variants, although only a subset requires independent confirmation for clinical interpretation. Sanger sequencing remains the standard confirmation method but is impractical for large-scale variant verification. We developed and evaluated a strategy for variant confirmation based on multi-amplicon massively parallel sequencing of pooled DNA samples. Whole-genome sequencing data were obtained from 86 individuals, including patients with parkinsonism and controls. Variants were selected using phenotype-driven filtering, ClinVar classification, and pathogenicity assessment criteria. A total of 307 variants were targeted using a custom amplicon panel comprising 290 amplicons. DNA samples were normalized, pooled into 16 mixtures, and sequenced following automated library preparation. Variant presence and sequencing quality were assessed using standard bioinformatic tools. Of the 307 selected variants, 243 were successfully confirmed. Unconfirmed variants included sequencing artifacts (18), insufficiently covered targets (5), large insertions or deletions exceeding 12 base pairs (36), and variants located within homopolymeric regions (5). Results for selected variants were concordant with Sanger sequencing, and observed variant frequencies corresponded to expected frequencies in pooled samples. This approach provides a robust, rapid, and cost-effective method for high-throughput genetic variants confirming identified by whole-genome sequencing while requiring only limited DNA input. Despite complete concordance with Sanger sequencing, larger validation studies are needed before multi-amplicon massively parallel sequencing can replace routine confirmatory testing.
n7717752186fb: *Background*: Non-communicable diseases driven by unhealthy lifestyles are a growing and largely avoidable burden among industrial workers. Patient-level evidence on the effectiveness of structured lifestyle programmes delivered alongside standard care - such as a traffic-light dietary guideline, a Yoga protocol and a daily four-spice culinary extract - remains limited. The Integrative Health Clinic (IHC) at ESIC Medical College & Hospital, Faridabad, India, is a family-medicine-style outpatient clinic that follows the 21-item Health Building Lifestyle Guideline and delivers care through a 7-step COM-B-based protocol. We therefore estimated patient-reported relief and compliance with three lifestyle practices in patients attending the IHC. *Methods*: We conducted a retrospective single-arm cohort of patients first seen between February 2025 and 30 September 2026, with follow-up through 4 November 2026. All patients received the three-component lifestyle intervention (advice on spice extract, diet and Yoga) and were offered follow-up; the 1,466 patients with a usable telephone contact were called for feedback and reinforcement of practices. A physical visit with a coded diagnosis was treated as a valid record. Each patient called was coded once for relief and for spice, diet and Yoga compliance using the most recent definitive answer (YES/NO); calls without a definitive answer ("no response", "not interested") were skipped, and patients with no definitive answer on any call were classified as such. Disease burden, including the screening-detected diagnoses, was counted as patient-condition pairs and classed into 14 systems. *Results*: There were 4,047 valid visit records from 1,737 unique patients (904 female [52.0%]; mean age 40.3 +/- 14.6 years; 833 male [48.0%]; mean age 44.8 +/- 15.1 years). Of these, there were 1,035 single-visit [59.6%] and 702 revisit patients [40.4%], i.e. 2.33 visits per patient. The 1,466 analysed patients (763 female [52.1%] and 703 male [47.9%]) comprised 666 revisit and 800 single-visit patients. Their most frequent patient-condition pairs were hypertension (511), obesity (397) and arthritis (268); objective-evidence screening contributed 246 pairs in 233 patients (obesity 161, hypertension 39, anaemia 44, diabetes 2). Of the 1,466 (84.4% of 1,737) patients with a usable telephone contact who were called, 1,016 had a definitive relief answer: 850 (83.7%; 95% CI 81.3-85.8) reported relief and 166 reported no relief. The remaining 450 had no definitive answer. Among the 1,016 patients with a definitive answer, relief was 87.2% (395/453) in revisit versus 80.8% (455/563) in single-visit patients. Treating all 450 patients without a definitive relief answer as no relief, the conservative lower bound of patients reporting relief was 58.0% overall (850/1,466), 59.3% in revisit (395/666) and 56.9% in single-visit patients (455/800). Among the 1,016 patients with practice data, compliance with the spice extract, diet and Yoga was 77.1%, 83.3% and 81.2%, respectively; counting all 450 non-responders as non-compliant gave conservative estimates of 53.4%, 57.7% and 56.3% for the three practices (n = 1,466). In the responding cohort, relief rose with the five-level compliance dose, from 5.2% (6/115) at dose 0 to 98.2% (326/332) at dose 4 (all three practices plus a repeat visit). *Conclusions*: In this exploratory single-arm cohort, patient-reported relief was more frequent at higher levels of a composite measure that combined the three practices and repeat visits. Because there was no comparison group and all lifestyle components were delivered jointly alongside continuing pharmacotherapy, causality cannot be inferred. The findings support feasibility and justify prospective, controlled, disease-specific studies. The efficacy of the four-spice extract remains under study and is not yet a proven treatment.
n6946ca9a19cf: Introduction. Nepal's routine health information system runs on DHIS2, but no published data-quality assessment covers its mountainous districts. The method raises a second issue: the WHO Data Quality Review (DQR) tests internal consistency partly through related-indicator pairs, assuming each indicator is recorded independently. DHIS2 validation rules act on paired values at entry, so a rule-governed pair may agree for reasons unrelated to recording quality. Methods. In this study, a WHO DQR Module 1 desk review was conducted on aggregated DHIS2 data from all 132 facilities in Sankhuwasabha district, analysed at district and local level (palika) resolution: seven datasets for completeness and timeliness, and 17 tracer indicators for internal consistency, for fiscal year 2081/82 (2024/25) against the three preceding years (2021/22 to 2023/24). Pairs were classified in advance as rule-governed or free, and three denominator-free ratios compared with Nepal Demographic and Health Survey (NDHS) 2022 estimates for Koshi Province. Results. Completeness was at least 90.6% in every dataset and unit. Timeliness fell below 90% in 22 of 70 unit-dataset combinations, concentrated in four remote local levels. Of four rule-governed pairs only iron and deworming changed materially, 1.42 to 1.00; two never agreed, indicating rules that query rather than block entry. The free pairs diverged: Penta-1 to Penta-3 dropout fell from +3.6% to -5.4%, negative in 9 of 10 local levels, and BCG was below Penta-1 in 8 of 10. District totals were inverted at both steps (BCG 1,537, Penta-1 1,666, Penta-3 1,756), which redistribution cannot produce. Conclusion. Reporting is nearly complete, but the data carry a persistent immunization anomaly that completeness and timeliness miss, pointing to a systematic recording process. Because a rule-governed pair may agree by configuration, DHIS2 assessments should classify pairs against the active validation-rule set before interpretation.
n19aeee06215e: Objective: Uterine dyscontractility plays a major role in pain sensation, infertility, and adenomyosis pathogenesis. In vivo, contractility occurs in the inner myometrium and junctional zone, which is thickened in adenomyosis. We examined whether the junctional zone presents particular contractile features ex vivo by measuring contractility and oxytocin response in full-thickness serosa-to-endometrium myometrial slices retrieved from control and adenomyosis patients. Design: Prospective ex vivo case-control study. Subjects: Premenopausal women following hysterectomy: adenomyosis (n = 16) and controls (n = 12). Contractility: 57 strips (11 vs 8 patients), immunofluorescence: 10 vs 9 patients. Main Outcome Measures: We resorted to spatiotemporal mapping, time-lapse video-based techniques used in the field of gastroenterology. We measured contraction frequency, amplitude, duration, velocity, site of origin, and propagation direction along the serosa-to-endometrium axis, before and after oxytocin. We measured oxytocin receptor density along the serosa-to-endometrium axis by immunofluorescence and machine learning-assisted segmentation. Results: Ex vivo contractile waves propagated throughout the outer and inner myometrium, with similar amplitude and frequency. Contraction frequency, amplitude, duration, and velocity did not differ between control and adenomyosis uteri. Oxytocin increased contraction frequency and velocity and systematically caused contractile waves to originate at the inner myometrium in both groups. In both groups, oxytocin receptor density was highest in the inner myometrium. Adenomyosis patients had a 1.8-fold higher oxytocin receptor density, but a smaller oxytocin-induced increase in contraction frequency. Conclusion: We provide the first ex vivo spatiotemporal time-lapse analysis of myometrial contractions. The whole myometrium contracts ex vivo, not just the inner part (junctional zone). This uniform myogenic motility is presumably inhibited neurally in vivo in the outer myometrium. Ex vivo adenomyosis basal contractility was similar to that of controls. Adenomyotic myometrium overexpressed oxytocin receptors compared to controls, but this did not translate into a stronger contractile response to oxytocin. In both groups, oxytocin caused contractile waves to originate at and propagate from the sub-endometrial myometrium, where receptor density is higher. This demonstrates that contractile wave direction can be controlled hormonally.
n59cd5175323e: Distinct tau-vulnerable and relatively spared subregions exist within the medial temporal lobe (MTL). However, it remains unclear that how functional connectivity (FC), anchored to tau-vulnerable MTL subregions, is related to tau pathology, synaptic dysfunction, and cognitive decline across the Alzheimer's disease (AD) continuum. We here probe into this with resting-state fMRI data from a discovery cohort (ADNI; N = 386; cognitively normal [CN], mild cognitive impairment [MCI], and AD; 144 with 2-year follow-up) and an independent validation cohort at local hospital (N = 100; CN, subjective cognitive decline [SCD], and MCI; 25 receiving high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation [HF-rTMS]). We first separated the MTL into subregions with high and low neurofibrillary tangle (NFT) burden based on histological atlases, and calculated the seed-based whole-brain FC for each subregion. Second, group differences were assessed using ANCOVA, and associations with amyloid-{beta} (A{beta})/tau pathology, synaptic biomarkers, and cognitive performance were examined. Third, serial mediation, cross-lagged, and longitudinal regression analyses were performed to investigate the proposed pathological sequence, with additional evidence from HF-rTMS intervention and autopsy-confirmed Braak staging. Our results showed that, with the development of AD, FC reductions were focused on the high-NFT MTL network, particularly involving the inferior temporal gyrus and precuneus. Baseline tau burden in high-NFT MTL regions was able to predict subsequent FC alterations. Interestingly, FC between the high-NFT MTL and global brain showed region-specific associations with synaptic biomarkers, including negative associations in the cerebellum and positive associations in the precentral gyrus. We also observed a divergent association between the FC and cognition or pathology at different AD stages, shifting from positive in the early stages to negative in advanced AD. Serial mediation analyses supported a pathway linking tau burden to cognitive impairment through altered high-NFT MTL connectivity in the precuneus and occipital regions and subsequent synaptic dysfunction. Cross-lagged and longitudinal analyses further confirmed the proposed temporal sequence. Furthermore, HF-rTMS-related cognitive improvements were partially associated with enhanced synaptic plasticity through changes in precuneus-high-NFT MTL connectivity. Collectively, these findings support a spatiotemporal framework linking the dysfunction of tau-vulnerable MTL network to synaptic impairment and cognitive decline, highlighting high-NFT MTL-based FC as a potential imaging marker tracking AD progression.
nf1e27765bb77: Lung cancer remains the leading cause of cancer‑related mortality, yet the role of lower airway microbiota in disease development and progression is incompletely defined. Here, we characterised the lung microbiome in an Australian cohort (lung cancer n =106, healthy n =10) using shotgun metagenomics and semi‑quantitative culture to evaluate site-specific microbial ecology across the tumour microenvironment (TME), contralateral airways, and oral cavity, to evaluate microbiome differences across early‑ and late‑stage disease, and to quantify clinical covariate impacts on airway microbiota. Diversity analyses, multivariable linear modelling, and culture‑based comparisons were performed, with adjustment for smoking pack‑years, sex, and tumour characteristics. Cumulative smoking exposure caused significant, progressive core commensal depletion ( Neisseria subflava , Gemella sanguinis , Rothia mucilaginosa ), alongside Streptococcus mitis enrichment, with Mogibacterium diversum uniquely depleted within the TME of smokers. β diversity in both early- and late-stage bronchial washes (BWs) significantly diverged from healthy controls, whilst Shannon diversity (α diversity) was significantly reduced in early-stage compared with late-stage BWs. The early‑stage TME also demonstrated significantly reduced microbial cultivability compared with healthy and other lung cancer BWs. A small number of taxa were uniquely enriched ( Sporothrix and Pseudomonas species) or depleted ( Streptococcus parasanguinis , Streptococcus cristatus , R. mucilaginosa ) within the TME, and 13 taxa were significantly enriched or depleted in both TME and contralateral airways compared with healthy airways. Only lung adenocarcinoma showed distinct oral β‑diversity restructuring. Taken together, our findings demonstrate that the lung cancer microbiome is characterised by early and progressive lower airway dysbiosis that is strongly shaped by tumour presence. Our findings point to potential new avenues for microbiome‑based diagnostic and therapeutic strategies.
nb5f484d69cfa: Importance: Payment policy for clinical artificial intelligence (AI) is changing quickly, yet national data on which AI-enabled services are used, and for whom, are limited. Objective: To describe national trends in the use of AI-related Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes and how use differs by patient, geographic, and payer characteristics. Design, Setting, and Participants: This serial cross-sectional study used Epic Cosmos, a deidentified electronic health record dataset, to examine 11,605,867,309 encounters among 233,628,292 US patients from January 1, 2021, to April 14, 2026. Exposures: Calendar year, age, sex, race, ethnicity, rurality, area-level social vulnerability, census region, and primary payer. Main Outcomes and Measures: Encounters with any of 65 CPT codes that require AI, identified by matching the CPT code set to US Food and Drug Administration-listed AI-enabled devices and classified as assistive, augmentative, or autonomous using the CPT Appendix S taxonomy. Results: Of 11.6 billion encounters, 335,349 (2.9 per 100,000) included an AI-required CPT code. The odds of an encounter with an AI-required code were 9.88 (95% CI, 9.71-10.06) times higher in 2025 than in 2021. In unadjusted comparisons, use was higher among patients aged 65 to 85 years and among those with Medicare (OR, 5.11) or Medicare Advantage (OR, 5.12) vs commercial insurance. Use was lower among Black (OR, 0.72) and Hispanic or Latino (OR, 0.34) patients, Medicaid enrollees (OR, 0.65), residents of the most socially vulnerable areas (OR, 0.53), and residents of the most rural areas (OR, 0.86). Use of automated diabetic retinopathy screening increased after the service was added to a HEDIS quality measure. One newer code (quantitative brain MRI) appeared in rural areas within months of becoming effective, whereas older codes such as retinopathy screening took years. Conclusions and Relevance: In this cross-sectional study, billed use of AI-enabled services remained rare but grew substantially and was concentrated among older and Medicare-insured patients, with lower use among Medicaid enrollees and residents of socially vulnerable areas. As the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services restructures payment for software and launches outcome-based models, tracking who receives AI-enabled care across payment pathways will be important for equitable access.
nce2a8ff774e3: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is the de facto method for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large neural networks, achieving strong task adaptation with minimal trainable parameters and low optimization cost. Beyond this efficiency, practitioners have observed two striking properties: \textit{robustness to catastrophic forgetting} and the ability to \textit{merge independently trained adapters} into a single model that performs competitively across multiple tasks. These properties are central to continual and multi-task learning, yet remain poorly understood. In this work, we provide a theoretical explanation through a unified \textit{margin-based perspective}. We analyze LoRA in multiclass linear classification under a near-orthogonal task regime with $\ell_2$-regularization, and characterize the optimal LoRA adapter across regularization regimes. Our analysis shows that, in an intermediate regime of regularization parameters, the optimal adapter aligns with the \emph{max-margin solution} on the fine-tuning data. Building on this characterization, we derive two key consequences. First, we obtain closed-form expressions for the margins on pre-training and fine-tuning data, revealing a precise margin trade-off: the regularization parameter controls the balance between retention and adaptation. Second, we analyze adapter merging, proving that merged models achieve positive margin on each task and deriving optimal mixing coefficients that balance margins across tasks and maximize the margin over their union. These results lead to a simple, training-free merging rule, which we term \textit{margin-based LoRA merging} (MaLoRA). Experiments on modern architectures and real datasets validate our theoretical predictions, showing that MaLoRA matches or outperforms several adapter-merging baselines across a range of vision and language classification tasks.
n88c14d6aa9b5: Cross-validation estimates predictive performance by repeatedly splitting the data into training and validation sets, fitting the model on the first and evaluating it on the second. Every observation influences the estimate in two roles, through its own evaluation when it is held out and through the models it helps fit when it trains. The random splits determine its weight in each role. From this representation, we prove an exact finite-sample identity for the variance of the cross-validated estimate. For a given splitting scheme with a common training set size, the variance is a function of these weights, with constants of the model, the metric, and the population. It covers metrics averaged over observations, such as mean squared error, and over case--control pairs, such as the AUC. The identity shows which schemes to use. The variance decomposes into sampling variance, which depends only on the training size, and variance due to the random fold splitting, which arises when the weights change from one draw of the splits to the next. K-fold cross-validation, whose weights are equal across observations by design, is therefore variance optimal at first order; Monte Carlo and bootstrap cross-validation are not. The first-order variance of K-fold does not depend on K, and under reasonable conditions on the model leave-one-out has the smallest variance of any K-fold scheme. For the AUC the same holds for leave-pair-out, which evaluates every case--control pair. Finally, we show the cross-validated estimate is asymptotically normal with the identity's full variance. Together, these results provide a general theoretical foundation for inference on cross-validated performance and establish principles for selecting variance-optimal cross-validation designs.
nb0bdde1966d0: Policy optimization is central to language model post-training, yet principled guidance remains limited. We revisit its theoretical foundations to identify algorithms that learn near-optimal policies using total samples and gradient steps governed by the base model's response coverage, a measure of how readily it generates optimal responses. We call such algorithms coverage-preserving. This guarantee captures the goal of amplifying capabilities accessible through sampling from the base model. (1) Coverage collapse. REINFORCE, the basis for PPO and GRPO, can drive the probability of optimal responses to near zero, even as reward improves. This coverage collapse stalls optimization, and convergence can require exponentially many steps despite good initial coverage. The failure arises even with exact gradients and persists under KL regularization to the base model. (2) Reference resets. We show that repeatedly resetting the KL reference to the most recent policy mitigates coverage collapse. We formalize this intervention in Approximate Policy Mirror Descent (APMD), a meta-algorithm that approximately solves a sequence of KL-regularized RL subproblems. APMD enables stronger regularization, making each subproblem easier to solve, while reference resets allow convergence to global optimality. (3) Coverage-preserving algorithms. For softmax linear policies over pretrained features, we use APMD to establish the first global convergence guarantees showing that widely used families of post-training algorithms are coverage-preserving. These include stylized PPO and GRPO variants with explicit KL regularization and reference resets, and squared-loss algorithms that implement them implicitly, including those used to train the Kimi models. These results clarify how regularization, clipping, and objective choice affect the sampling and optimization costs of post-training.
n3da19bab9c03: Users often complain that AI assistants such as ChatGPT are getting worse. Some versions do change, but human evaluation leaves a second possibility untested: the people judging may change. We separate the two on Chatbot Arena, a public platform where people compare answers from two anonymous large language models (LLMs) and pick the better one or say both are bad. We study 1,260,967 blind votes cast from May 2023 to August 2024 on pairs of models whose versions are fixed: dated vendor snapshots and models with fixed open weights. For the same pair of unchanged models, the share of votes saying "both are bad" rises by 1.71 percentage points a month on a mean of 17.1%, and by 1.91 points a month in 2024. In fourteen pairs observed often in both 2023 and 2024, it rose in every one, from 15.5% to 23.3%. The ranking does not trend: in 2024, the stronger model's share of decisive votes is flat. The rise holds within the same voter and on the same pair, and across arrival cohorts from their first recorded vote. It holds with prompt controls, in every major language, for dated vendor snapshots, open-weight models and models with stable answer length, and between interface changes. The drift is shared across models: month effects estimated from other models' pairs remove it from each model's own pairs. Platform-wide, the average model would be expected to score 78% against the 2023 average, yet the share of "both are bad" votes ended near where it began. The pattern fits a standard that follows the category's progress, so a product that stands still is judged as declining. Absolute verdicts on AI drifted while relative comparisons held steady, an evaluation drift that matters for LLM leaderboards and for the human feedback used to train models.
naef52cbb17ca: Research agents achieve increasingly strong benchmark scores, yet these scores do not necessarily translate into reliable delivery in ongoing research projects. Many research-agent benchmarks emphasize standalone tasks and relatively self-contained workflows in clean or curated workspaces. However, researchers ask agents to complete one step within an ongoing project, where requests depend on earlier session decisions and workspaces contain unfinished files, outdated versions, and failed attempts. We introduce ARE-bench to evaluate whether research agents advance ongoing projects while respecting prior decisions and existing workspace state, grounded in real session context and in-progress workspaces. ARE-bench includes 75 tasks built on agent sessions and full workspaces from recruited researchers' own projects, spanning seven research stages, 33 requirements, and 150 sub-requirements, with 1,173 binary checklist items in total. Each task is anchored at a real user request, preserves its requirements, and summarizes the earlier requests still in effect as background. The complete workspace is replayed to that boundary without cleanup, preserving artifacts from earlier turns. Each checklist is compiled from an intent-aligned rubric and credits any valid solution. Across seven frontier models, the strongest passes every checklist item on only 66.2% of tasks, and Design and Execution rank among the hardest stages for every model. Three models pass about 69% of tasks when only delivery contracts and general norms are checked, but just 28.4% to 40.0% once historical and material or workspace requirements are also checked. Evaluating delivery without these contextual requirements can therefore overestimate research agents and mask differences between them.
n1d89378429ce: We use TabPFN, a recently developed tabular foundation model, to predict three properties of energetic materials: impact sensitivity, decomposition temperature and crystal density. Without any hyperparameter tuning, TabPFN outperforms the best published models for all three properties. It also substantially outperforms a wide range of established machine-learning models, including tuned gradient boosting (XGBoost), random forests and Gaussian processes. This holds both when the models are given hand-crafted molecular descriptors and when they are given learned representations from Chemprop's message-passing neural network. In particular, for all three properties, TabPFN applied to Chemprop's own embedding is more accurate than Chemprop's predictions. TabPFN is also among the fastest models we consider, more than an order of magnitude faster than XGBoost. As TabPFN predicts the entire distribution of the target rather than just a single value, it offers built-in uncertainty quantification, which we compare with the empirical distributions of compounds with repeated measurements. Finally, we interpret the predictions using Shapley values, which rank the features by their importance.
n9e21f111fcb9: Energy-based models (EBMs) define a distribution through a scalar energy, $p_θ(x)\propto\exp(-E_θ(x))$, and are usually presented as one model family among many. This tutorial has a broader goal: beyond introducing EBMs, it uses them as a single lens that connects the different aspects of machine learning. Any EBM is specified by three choices, the energy, which determines what the model represents; the inference procedure, which samples from or optimizes the energy; and the learning method, which fits the energy to data. We first develop these components, including sampling, variational inference, and learning by maximum likelihood, noise contrastive estimation, pseudolikelihood, score matching, and adversarial training, and show that the learning methods share one contrastive structure. We then show that discriminative models, generative models such as GANs, normalizing flows, diffusion and autoregressive models, representation learning methods such as contrastive learning, word2vec, BERT, denoising auto-encoders, and diffusion representations, reinforcement learning with EBM policies and world models, inverse reinforcement learning, and planning, as well as inference-time computation with verifiers, are all EBMs that differ in these three choices, mostly in how they handle the partition function and sampling. This view explains existing methods, organizes them into a common framework, and suggests new algorithms by replacing one component while keeping the others, with composition of energies as a principled way to combine learned models at inference time.
ne526c3ed2070: Language-model systems use self-judgment to decide which answers to release, review, or recompute. Because intervention is costly, an assurance score must rank errors well at the available budget, not merely over the full ranking. We compare the judge's continuous verdict-token score with a supervised correctness probe trained on attention-head activations from the same prompt. Exact identities link fixed-budget error recall to residual risk and show that AUROC averages recall over all budgets. Across three open 7-12B models on GSM8K and MATH, the probe finds 1.3-22.5 additional percentage points of errors at 5% review in all six model-dataset settings (median 7.4 points). At 10% routing, probe-guided allocation improves accuracy over equal-cost random allocation in both GSM8K experiments, but beats judge-guided routing only for the weaker judge. Cross-dataset transfer lowers probe AUROC for every model in both directions relative to target-domain training. Because dataset, weight precision, and generation budget change together, this measures a joint protocol shift rather than a dataset-only effect. Internal signals can improve supervised, in-domain budget allocation, but are not domain-general confidence estimators.
n63d02d546653: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) produces rich training experience, yet outcome rewards reduce each attempt to a single number and leave most of this information unused. Training-time scaffolds, such as strategies or hints added to the prompt during training, offer a natural way to turn this information into guidance, but their design and adaptation are largely left to humans and tailored to specific domains. We introduce AutoScaffold, a unified AI-for-AI framework that turns a student's training experience into adaptive scaffolds, with minimal domain-specific information and no human intervention during training. A frozen teacher periodically examines this experience, diagnoses bottlenecks, and designs scaffolds in two forms: (i) strategies shared across a class of tasks and (ii) hints for individual hard tasks, adjusting the content and amount of support as the student learns. The scaffolds are removed at evaluation. We apply the same framework to ALFWorld, search-based QA, mathematical reasoning, and GPU kernel generation. When evaluated without scaffolds, students trained with AutoScaffold outperform those trained with the corresponding RL baselines in all four domains, with gains of 7.2 points in ALFWorld success and 4.0 points in average QA exact match. On GPU kernel generation, AutoScaffold increases the fraction of tasks with a correct kernel that runs faster than the PyTorch reference by up to 5.0 points. On math, our student surpasses QuestA's reported accuracy using approximately one-third as many student training steps. Analyses show that the teacher identifies a different failure in each task class and shifts its scaffolds from step-by-step workflows to targeted fixes as the student improves, and that its revised scaffolds help the student learn more than keeping the previous scaffold or using no scaffold.
n7f85eb8f1df8: We study Bayesian inference of persistence from early observations of a heterogeneous susceptible--infected--susceptible (SIS) reaction--diffusion model with standard incidence. We show that the leading prevalence dynamics depend on the unknown coefficients only through the difference between the transmission and recovery rates and the infected diffusivity. The same pair determines the principal eigenvalue whose sign governs persistence, so early prevalence can inform the threshold even when the individual rates remain uncertain. We prove global weak well-posedness and quantitative parameter stability for the SIS system and use the resulting observation-map estimates to establish Bayesian well-posedness. For an initial infection of size $\varepsilon$, we derive a uniform second-order expansion that describes how the separate rates enter prevalence. Incidence depends explicitly on transmission at leading order. When the noise standard deviation is proportional to $\varepsilon$, we prove $O(\varepsilon)$ convergence in Hellinger distance of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits for both prevalence alone and joint prevalence and incidence data. We bound the principal eigenvalue using the growth rate of the infected $L^2$ norm between two times. This rate gives a lower bound for the full nonlinear system, and the upper bound separates spatial transients from nonlinear saturation. Uniform spectral estimates and bounds on infection size and measurement error give sufficient conditions for persistence and extinction. We also bound the error in posterior persistence probabilities under forward and eigenvalue approximation, accounting for posterior mass near the threshold. Numerical examples illustrate threshold inference and the predicted \(O(\varepsilon)\) convergence of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits in Hellinger distance.
n8e320a392b8b: Local language models can save memory by storing weights in fewer bits, and they can reduce sensitivity to the order of answer options by averaging a few reorderings. We ask whether the first makes the second worse, and which is the cheaper way to spend a fixed budget. On Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen3-1.7B with simulated round-to-nearest weight quantization (8, 6, 4 and 3 bits, fp16 reference), read from the logits of the letters A to D on ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, MMLU and HellaSwag (300 items each), 6 bits lose no accuracy against fp16 (they score +1.8 (+1.0 to +2.5) and +0.9 (+0.3 to +1.5) points higher, which we do not explain), and 8 bits change it by -0.7 (-1.1 to -0.3) and -0.4 (-0.7 to -0.2) points. At 4 bits the answer-slot skew rises from 0.15 to 0.53 (0.6B) and from 0.07 to 0.12 (1.7B); Gaussian noise at the same weight SNR gives 0.15 and 0.37 (two draws) and 0.19 (one draw), so the control is inconclusive on whether rounding adds slot skew beyond equal-power noise. Flip rates rise but stay below an accuracy-matched baseline of independent uniform errors. Averaging four cyclic orders recovers +12.6 points at 4 bits for 0.6B (+5.3 at fp16). We price bits and passes in one machine-independent unit, weight bytes read times passes. In cost-matched pairs, extra orders beat extra bits only when the weights have 6 or more bits, and the decision table reduces to: use 6-bit weights and spend the rest of the budget on up to four orders, one pass each. Everything is simulated on two small models with the simplest quantizer; a title-level search found no earlier study of quantization together with option order.
nfeb6794c307d: Diffusion Language Models (DLMs) have emerged as effective alternatives to autoregressive models for latency-critical tasks, enabling faster token generation. Recent advances employ block diffusion with self-editing capabilities, where each block refines tokens iteratively before advancing to the next one. Yet each block is only as fast as its slowest token, and the next block cannot start before it. We suggest Blurring the Block Boundaries (B3), a novel method with which two blocks are refined in parallel within a shared forward pass. B3 calibrates itself on the fly, opening the next block only once the model is ready to start generating it. It is a training-free and hyperparameter-free acceleration method which seamlessly integrates within any self-editing block diffusion model. Evaluated on state-of-the-art DLMs across 10 diverse datasets spanning varied tasks and difficulty levels, B3 results in on par generation quality and 11.5-14.5% speedup compared to the base model, pushing the Pareto frontier for latency-quality trade-offs in DLM inference.
nd0ba05b52185: Visual Question Answering (VQA) imposes substantial computational overhead on vision-language models (VLMs), motivating model-agnostic input reduction methods that can be readily applied across diverse VLMs, including in black-box settings. Simply enforcing a visual-token cap reduces computation, but it can discard information needed to answer the question. A single reduction strategy also struggles to accommodate different scenarios. Our key observation is that cropping and compression are complementary: cropping highlights small targets and local details, whereas whole-image compression better preserves context for large targets or distributed evidence. Based on this observation, we propose C$^2$-Routing, which adaptively selects cropping or compression according to the input image and question. Since both strategies may still discard key information, we further design a safety gate that uses the predicted joint correctness distribution under original and reduced inputs to guide fallback and protect accuracy. To accommodate consumer GPU resource constraints, all training and evaluation experiments run on RTX 3090 GPUs. To measure gains beyond token capping, we use full-image baselines with the same cap of 1,024 visual tokens. We conduct extensive evaluation on three VLMs and 18 datasets spanning local details, global scenes, scene text, and documents. With the visual budget already capped, C$^2$-Routing further reduces end-to-end FLOPs by 36.53% and visual tokens by 42.36% on average, with a mean relative task-score decrease of only 0.77%.
nb4ef1bf593b3: Retrieval-augmented systems often retrieve passages that are accurate and relevant but state the answer at a coarser level of granularity than the question requires. For example, a question may ask which specific disease a drug treats (familial hyperlipidemia), while the retrieved passage mentions the broader disease family (hyperlipidemia). Prior work on context sufficiency treats such coarse passages simply as insufficient. We argue that they form a distinct case, which we call resolvable insufficiency: text alone cannot settle the fine-grained answer, but the broader category it mentions maps to a short list of candidate answers in a domain ontology. When language models read these coarse, family-only passages, they exhibit a phenomenon we call Clade (Category-Level Answering from Deficient Evidence): they answer instead of abstaining or searching further. On biomedical questions from PrimeKG, family-only passages reduce abstention by 13.8 points compared to uninformative passages, and the resulting guesses are wrong about half the time. A counterfactual test confirms the cause: replacing an exact disease name with its broader family name lowers abstention by 17.4 points compared to deleting the sentence. Simple fixes like confidence filtering, scaling to a larger model, and explicitly instructing the model to abstain cannot resolve Clade, and this replicates on ecological species interactions in GloBI. Finally, we test whether an ontology can turn coarse passages into exact answers. Given the correct family, an ontology list includes the true answer in 98.5% of cases, but string matching finds that family on the page for only 19.8%. Letting the model choose the family raises this to 30.0% and end-to-end recovery from 10.0% to 26.8%. Overall, our results show when language models should stop guessing and consult an ontology, and highlight which steps of that process remain unsolved.
n3209c45b7955: Concept-based explanations in neural models are important for the development, certification, and adoption of autonomous systems. Yet, interpretability remains correlational. Without methods to guide and quantify causal relationships between explanations, a concept explanation can be provided without being necessary or sufficient for the observed output thereby appearing correct while misleading. We introduce Causal Concept Wrapper Network (CCW-Net), the first use of interventional mediation analysis from fields such as economics, medicine, and epidemiology as a training objective to align causal effects of concept-based explanations with a model's output. We further apply mediation analysis as an evaluation tool to quantify, per concept label combination, how much of any model's output is causally attributable to each concept explanation. As a training objective, CCW-Net shapes a model's concept representations such that they are both necessary and sufficient for the outputs they are credited with and independent of other concepts' contributions. Counterfactual concept representations anchor a set of causal alignment criteria: necessity, sufficiency, and independence. Necessity drives irrelevant concept effects toward zero, sufficiency ensures relevant concept representations fully reconstruct a model's output, and independence enforces the total effect decomposes linearly across concepts. We evaluate CCW-Net across aircraft control, driving, and image classification. CCW-Net provides a step toward concept-based explanations that are not merely interpretable, but quantifiably causal, supporting safer evaluation, certification, and deployment of transparent and trustworthy neural models.
n8cc51896f13f: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly exhibit capabilities that resemble human Learning by Thinking (LbT), the acquisition of new insight through internal processes such as explanation and reasoning, without new external input. A systematic account of the cognitive mechanisms behind these capabilities, and of their limits, remains underdeveloped. This paper proposes a Cognitive LbT Framework that maps four mechanisms (Reflective Reasoning, Synthetic Memory Formation, Internal Simulation, and Conceptual Self-Organization) onto computational processes in LLMs. Drawing on representative methods, including chain-of-thought prompting, self-consistency, self-reflection, Tree-of-Thoughts search, Self-Instruct, and self-taught reasoning, the analysis argues that selected methods can functionally approximate aspects of these mechanisms and can improve performance on some tasks without additional labeled examples, although this does not always constitute durable learning in model parameters. For example, Self-Instruct generated approximately 52,000 instructions from 175 seed tasks and reported a 33% absolute improvement on Super-NaturalInstructions (Y. Wang et al., 2023). The same mechanisms also produce characteristic failures, including hallucination diffusion, model collapse, concept drift, and high computational cost. These failures are not isolated technical defects but follow from four structural asymmetries between LLMs and human cognition: the identity of generator and monitor, closed learning loops without external grounding, symbolic rather than sensorimotor simulation, and the cost of inference-time computation. The framework yields testable propositions about when LbT in LLMs should succeed or fail and offers a structured basis for designing more reliable autonomous learning systems.
nb7096bd95203: Deploying LLM-based analytics agents in enterprise settings requires evaluation frameworks that can reliably detect failures across complex, multi-tool workflows. We present a three-phase comparative study of three evaluation frameworks, each representing a distinct evaluation paradigm (trace-based LLM judging, text-only LLM judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics), applied to two analytics agents in a controlled research setting using frozen execution traces. Phase 1 quantifies evaluation harness stability through repeated measurements, finding that 97% of configurations meet the stability threshold and that stability patterns are agent-independent. Phase 2 measures known risk detection on 72 ground-truth test cases, where the trace-based framework achieves the best precision-recall balance (F1=0.90) while text-only evaluation matches on recall but generates 5x more false alarms. Phase 3 evaluates unknown risk discovery, uncovering 24 novel failures with zero overlap between functional testing and security red-teaming. Our results demonstrate that (1) the information available to the evaluation harness determines evaluation quality, (2) functional and security evaluation are complementary, and (3) LLM-based evaluation harnesses surface subtle errors that human reviewers miss. We recommend a two-framework strategy: trace-based evaluation for functional assessment and adversarial red-teaming for security validation.
n4df6fb98f01e: Agent harnesses have emerged as a promising mechanism for continual learning, alongside test-time parametric learning. However, the current benchmarks have several limitations: they generally focus on a single applied domain, serve each instance only once, and assume a single family of learner, so memory-based and weight-based systems are rarely compared on the same scale. We propose Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream built from the three ARC-AGI editions, whose tasks need no domain knowledge. The same tasks return after dormant gaps with fresh instances, while new tasks keep arriving. On each instance, the learner may pay for demonstrations, submit answers, or act inside the harness, with retries permitted on incorrect submissions, which are paid for. Each instance is scored based on the share of this feedback budget consumed. Since a learner may keep anything between instances, memory-based and weight-based systems are scored on the same scale. After the stream, the learner is frozen and tested on fresh instances of the tasks it met, which measures memorization, and on unseen tasks, which measures generalization. We run an agent harness with frozen weights, with and without persistence, on Qwen3.5-9B and GLM-5.3 Flash, comparing them with two prompting floors, a program-induction method and Qwen3.5-9B's weights trained to imitate GLM-5.3 Flash. Persistence in the harness generally does not improve memorization unless provided with explicit expert guidance. Most harness-based methods still learn less than a floor that simply caches each task's demonstrations, across all models we tested. No harness-based method gains on unseen tasks, whereas weight-based learning shows substantial gains. This opens the door to future weight-based continual learning that could teach models to drive harnesses in new domains.
